)}

<li><a href="#brief">Brief</a></li><li><a href="#explored">Explored</a></li><li><a href="#s">Cold Salvage</a></li><li><a href="#species">Species</a></li><li><a href="#map-a">Campaign map</a></li><li><a href="#r">The Salt Road</a></li><li><a href="#t">Tidewatch</a></li>
<li><a href="#compare">Compare</a></li><li><a href="#comparables">Comparables</a></li><li><a href="#recommendation">Recommendation</a></li><li><a href="#questions">Questions</a></li></ul></div></nav><header class="spread cover t-p" style="--bg:#0B0C0F"><div class="top"><div class="wrap">
<p class="eyebrow">Studio readout</p>
<h1>Project Haven:<span>Theme Exploration</span></h1>
<p class="sub">A studio readout after a month of exploration. Three themes for a Gloomhaven style tactics game, each with concept art, a rules mapping, a campaign, interface mockups, heroes, enemies and sample ability cards.</p>
<p class="meta">16 November 2026. All art is AI generated concept art. Nothing here has been playtested.</p></div></div>
<div class="tri"><div class="p"><div class="art img-s_key " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, key art for Cold Salvage" style="background-position:50% 62%"></div><div class="lab"><b>Cold Salvage</b><span>Space</span></div></div><div class="p"><div class="art img-r_key " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, key art for The Salt Road" style="background-position:50% 55%"></div><div class="lab"><b>The Salt Road</b><span>A caravan across a dead sea</span></div></div><div class="p"><div class="art img-t_key " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, key art for Tidewatch" style="background-position:50% 55%"></div><div class="lab"><b>Tidewatch</b><span>A drowned coast</span></div></div></div></header><section class="spread t-p contents" id="contents" aria-label="Contents"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Contents</p><h2>What is inside</h2></div><ol><li><a href="#brief"><i>01</i>Readout in brief<span>Three directions</span></a></li><li><a href="#explored"><i>02</i>What we explored<span>And what we threw away</span></a></li><li><a href="#s"><i>03</i>Cold Salvage<span>Space</span></a></li><li><a href="#species"><i>04</i>Species of the Ring<span>Six playable species</span></a></li><li><a href="#map-a"><i>05</i>Two campaign maps<span>Pick one</span></a></li><li><a href="#r"><i>06</i>The Salt Road<span>A caravan across a dead sea</span></a></li><li><a href="#t"><i>07</i>Tidewatch<span>A drowned coast</span></a></li><li><a href="#compare"><i>08</i>Side by side<span>Comparison</span></a></li><li><a href="#comparables"><i>09</i>Comparable games<span>Linked sources</span></a></li><li><a href="#recommendation"><i>10</i>Our recommendation<span>Next steps</span></a></li><li><a href="#questions"><i>11</i>Questions for you<span>Five challenges</span></a></li></ol></div></section><section class="spread t-p" id="brief"><div class="wrap">
<div class="grid2" style="align-items:end;margin-bottom:56px"><div class="sh" style="margin:0"><p class="eyebrow">Readout in brief</p><h2>Three directions, one recommendation</h2><p class="lead" style="margin-top:24px">We looked at the rules core as it stands and asked one question of every setting: what does this theme change about how the game is played? We kept three and wrote a full dossier for each.</p></div>
<div class="rec"><p class="eyebrow" style="margin:0">Our recommendation</p><p>Lead with Cold Salvage, on one condition: it must pass the swap test. In parallel, build the same first scenario as The Salt Road to prove the rules core is theme agnostic. If Cold Salvage fails the swap test, the Salt Road becomes the lead.</p></div></div>
<div class="cards3"><a class="tcard" href="#s" style="text-decoration:none"><div class="art img-s_key k169" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, key art for Cold Salvage" style="background-position:50% 62%"></div><span class="k">Theme one. Space</span><h4>Cold Salvage</h4><p style="font-size:15px;color:var(--muted)">A party of four, drawn from six species, strips the wrecks of a dead ring habitat around a dying red star. Salvage keeps the tow ship flying, and the cold always collects.</p></a><a class="tcard" href="#r" style="text-decoration:none"><div class="art img-r_key k169" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, key art for The Salt Road" style="background-position:50% 55%"></div><span class="k">Theme two. A caravan across a dead sea</span><h4>The Salt Road</h4><p style="font-size:15px;color:var(--muted)">Four guides lead a caravan across the Hollow Sea, a salt basin where a vanished empire left glass towers, walking machines and a heat that never quite stops moving.</p></a><a class="tcard" href="#t" style="text-decoration:none"><div class="art img-t_key k169" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, key art for Tidewatch" style="background-position:50% 55%"></div><span class="k">Theme three. A drowned coast</span><h4>Tidewatch</h4><p style="font-size:15px;color:var(--muted)">The lamps along the Hollow Coast are going out. Four keepers walk the tideline to relight them before the fog arrives with what the sea took.</p></a></div>
<p class="cap" style="margin-top:24px">Concept art, AI generated to set direction. None of it is final, and nothing here has been playtested.</p></div></section><section class="spread t-p" id="explored"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">What we explored</p><h2>How we got from many settings to three</h2></div>
<ol class="steps">
<li><b>Read the core and the design notes</b><span>We started from what the rules core already does and the design check in the notes: any system must work under two very different skins.</span></li>
<li><b>Sketched many settings</b><span>We wrote a one paragraph premise for each setting we could think of and tried to say what it changes in play.</span></li>
<li><b>Judged each against six checks</b><span>The swap test, core fit, campaign hook, art cost, distance from Gloomhaven and readability on a hex board.</span></li>
<li><b>Built three full dossiers</b><span>Concept art, rules mapping, campaign, scenarios, interface, heroes, enemies and cards for the three that survived.</span></li></ol>
<div class="tbl" style="margin-top:56px"><table><thead><tr><th>Check</th><th>The question</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td data-l="Check">Swap test</td><td data-l="The question">If we replace every theme noun with a fantasy equivalent, does the scenario still play the same? If so, the theme is a skin.</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Check">Core fit</td><td data-l="The question">How many changes does the theme ask of the rules core?</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Check">Campaign hook</td><td data-l="The question">Does the theme give the campaign a spine, a hub and a clock?</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Check">Art cost</td><td data-l="The question">How hard is the art to produce at a consistent look? This is our estimate.</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Check">Distance from Gloomhaven</td><td data-l="The question">Would a player see this as a different game, or a retheme of the original?</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Check">Board readability</td><td data-l="The question">Can a player read the board and the enemies at a glance on a hex grid?</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></section>
<section class="spread t-p" aria-label="What we threw away"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">What we threw away and why</p><h2>Five settings we set aside</h2></div>
<ul class="away"><li><b>Fallen gods and dark fantasy</b><span>The register Gloomhaven already owns. Its store page calls it a medieval dark fantasy universe. We would be compared on a depth of content we cannot match.</span><span class="pill">Set aside</span></li><li><b>Cyberpunk</b><span>The look depends on signage, rain and crowds, which read poorly on a hex board. Our judgement is that it fights the readability check.</span><span class="pill">Set aside</span></li><li><b>Wasteland</b><span>Visually close to Cold Salvage, without the pressure and air mechanics that give space something to do. It collapsed into the same board with less to say.</span><span class="pill">Set aside</span></li><li><b>Steampunk</b><span>Brass and gears are a subset of what the Salt Road’s glass machines already offer, and add no new mechanic.</span><span class="pill">Set aside</span></li><li><b>Pirates</b><span>A strong fantasy, but ships are the unit of play. Haven’s unit is one person on one hex.</span><span class="pill">Set aside</span></li></ul></div></section><section class="spread opener t-s" id="s"><div class="art cine img-s_key" role="img" aria-label="Concept art: a party of four, a human, a Durr, the Murmur and a Tikkri, walking toward a breach on a dead ring habitat" style="background-position:50% 78%"></div>
<div class="wrap"><div class="body"><div><p class="eyebrow">Theme one. Space</p><h2>Cold Salvage</h2><p class="hook">Six species. One dying ring. Every hull is a clock.</p><p class="lead" style="margin-top:18px">A party of four, drawn from six species, strips the wrecks of a dead ring habitat around a dying red star. Salvage keeps the tow ship flying, and the cold always collects.</p><p class="tone"><b>Tone.</b> Quiet, industrial and tense, with dry humour between the crew.</p></div>
<ol class="pillars"><li><span class="numl">1</span><div><b>The room is the enemy</b><span>Air, heat and pressure are board state. A compartment can kill you before anything shows up.</span></div></li><li><span class="numl">2</span><div><b>Every body is a different problem</b><span>Each species needs its suit for a different reason, and that reason becomes its class.</span></div></li><li><span class="numl">3</span><div><b>The ship is home</b><span>The tow ship Second Wind is the hub. Every repaired module is progress you can see.</span></div></li></ol></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s" id="space-case"><div class="wrap"><div class="grid2" style="gap:72px"><div><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Why this game</p><h2>Not fantasy with lasers</h2></div>
<p class="swap">Our test: swap every space noun for a fantasy one. If the scenario still plays the same, we cut it.</p>
<div class="ex"><div class="panel"><b>Fails</b><p>Kill six raiders with blasters. That is bandits with crossbows.</p></div><div class="panel"><b>Passes</b><p>Cut three bulkheads before the air runs out. Every hatch you open vents the room and drags everyone one hex toward it.</p></div></div></div>
<div class="pc pcpad"><h4>Why it wins</h4><ul><li>The room is the enemy, so the rules have work to do beyond damage.</li><li>Six alien body plans that no fantasy setting can do.</li><li>Hard surface art is modular: the cheapest of the three themes to keep consistent, by our estimate.</li></ul>
<h4>What it costs</h4><ul><li>The busiest genre of the three, with Phantom Epoch, Rogue Angels and Stars of Akarios already there.</li><li>Players expect guns, so guns stay short ranged and expensive.</li><li>Grey corridors get dull, so every sector gets its own look and hazard.</li></ul></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s" id="crew" aria-label="Cold Salvage: the starting crew"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">The playable crew</p><h3>Four starters, four species</h3><p class="lead" style="margin-top:16px;font-size:18px">Each class is one species. The Thren and the Sarn unlock later.</p></div>
<div class="crew"><article><div class="art img-sp_durr_suit " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Durr suited, the Breacher"></div><h4>Breacher</h4><p class="crew-species">The Durr</p><p class="d">Front line. Seals a doorway as a wall, and decompression cannot move it.</p></article><article><div class="art img-sp_human_suit " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Human suited, the Cutter"></div><h4>Cutter</h4><p class="crew-species">Human</p><p class="d">Melee damage. Torch cards create Heat that other cards spend.</p></article><article><div class="art img-sp_murmur_suit " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Murmur suited, the Tender"></div><h4>Tender</h4><p class="crew-species">The Murmur</p><p class="d">Healer and engineer. Sends out a scout cell as a summon.</p></article><article><div class="art img-sp_tikkri_suit " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Tikkri suited, the Runner"></div><h4>Runner</h4><p class="crew-species">The Tikkri</p><p class="d">Scout. Acts first, tethers allies and crawls through vents.</p></article></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s spopen" id="species" aria-label="Cold Salvage: species of the ring"><div class="wrap"><div class="sphead"><div class="sh" style="margin:0"><p class="eyebrow">Species of the Ring</p><h2>Change the body. The suit follows.</h2></div><p class="lead">Six species, each built around what its body cannot survive. The suit solves it, and the solution is the class.</p></div>
<div class="art img-sp_lineup k169" role="img" aria-label="Concept art lineup of six suited crew members to scale: a Tikkri, a human, a Thren, the Murmur, a Sarn and a Durr"></div>
<div class="lineuplab"><span style="left:7.5%">Tikkri</span><span style="left:19%">Human</span><span style="left:32%">Thren</span><span style="left:47%">Murmur</span><span style="left:65%">Sarn</span><span style="left:86%">Durr</span></div>
<p class="cap">Concept art, to scale from 60 centimetres to 3 metres. The Murmur suit is new: a walking hive, not a person shape.</p></div></section><section class="spread t-s" aria-label="Species: Humans and The Durr"><div class="wrap"><div class="sprow" id="species-human">
<div class="spimgs"><figure><div class="art img-sp_human_out k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Humans out of the suit"></div><figcaption>Out of the suit</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_human_suit k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Humans suited"></div><figcaption>Suited</figcaption></figure></div>
<div class="sptext"><h4>Humans</h4><p class="tag">The baseline</p><dl><div><dt>Body</dt><dd>Ring born bipeds who have never seen a planet.</dd></div><div><dt>The suit</dt><dd>Air, pressure and cold. The reference every other suit is measured against.</dd></div><div><dt>In play</dt><dd>Cutter. No species rule, so this class teaches the game.</dd></div></dl></div></div><div class="sprow" id="species-durr">
<div class="spimgs"><figure><div class="art img-sp_durr_out k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Durr out of the suit"></div><figcaption>Out of the suit</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_durr_suit k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Durr suited"></div><figcaption>Suited</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_durr_gear k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, gear for The Durr" style="background-size:cover"></div><figcaption>Hull jack</figcaption></figure></div>
<div class="sptext"><h4>The Durr</h4><p class="tag">Too strong for the ship</p><dl><div><dt>Body</dt><dd>A 3 metre quadruped from a heavy gravity world.</dd></div><div><dt>The suit</dt><dd>Ballast and braces, so light ship gravity does not make it lethal.</dd></div><div><dt>In play</dt><dd>Breacher. Anchored: immune to push, pull and decompression. The hull jack props doors open.</dd></div></dl></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s" aria-label="Species: The Thren and The Murmur"><div class="wrap"><div class="sprow" id="species-thren">
<div class="spimgs"><figure><div class="art img-sp_thren_out k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Thren out of the suit"></div><figcaption>Out of the suit</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_thren_suit k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Thren suited"></div><figcaption>Suited</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_thren_gear k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, gear for The Thren" style="background-size:cover"></div><figcaption>Brine lance</figcaption></figure></div>
<div class="sptext"><h4>The Thren</h4><p class="tag">A deep sea in a can</p><dl><div><dt>Body</dt><dd>Radial, five tentacles, from an ocean under ice.</dd></div><div><dt>The suit</dt><dd>A brass diving hull that holds crushing pressure in, not out.</dd></div><div><dt>In play</dt><dd>Unlock class. Pushes with pressurised brine, paid from its own pressure pool. A cracked dome works like a wound.</dd></div></dl></div></div><div class="sprow" id="species-murmur">
<div class="spimgs"><figure><div class="art img-sp_murmur_out k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Murmur out of the suit"></div><figcaption>Out of the suit</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_murmur_suit k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Murmur suited"></div><figcaption>Suited</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_murmur_gear k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, gear for The Murmur" style="background-size:cover"></div><figcaption>Scout cell</figcaption></figure></div>
<div class="sptext"><h4>The Murmur</h4><p class="tag">One crew member, hundreds of bodies</p><dl><div><dt>Body</dt><dd>A swarm of beetle moths that think together.</dd></div><div><dt>The suit</dt><dd>A walking hive on six legs. Every cell keeps one unit warm and breathing.</dd></div><div><dt>In play</dt><dd>Tender. Releases a scout cell as a summon. Health is counted in cells, so damage empties the frame.</dd></div></dl></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s" aria-label="Species: The Tikkri and The Sarn"><div class="wrap"><div class="sprow" id="species-tikkri">
<div class="spimgs"><figure><div class="art img-sp_tikkri_out k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Tikkri out of the suit"></div><figcaption>Out of the suit</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_tikkri_suit k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Tikkri suited"></div><figcaption>Suited</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_tikkri_gear k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, gear for The Tikkri" style="background-size:cover"></div><figcaption>Tail reel</figcaption></figure></div>
<div class="sptext"><h4>The Tikkri</h4><p class="tag">Fits where you do not</p><dl><div><dt>Body</dt><dd>60 centimetres, sticky toes, a prehensile tail.</dd></div><div><dt>The suit</dt><dd>A beetle shell that grips walls. At home, no floor ever stayed still.</dd></div><div><dt>In play</dt><dd>Runner. Lowest initiative in the game. Tethers allies, crawls through vents, clings to crates.</dd></div></dl></div></div><div class="sprow" id="species-sarn">
<div class="spimgs"><figure><div class="art img-sp_sarn_out k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Sarn out of the suit"></div><figcaption>Out of the suit</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_sarn_suit k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, The Sarn suited"></div><figcaption>Suited</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="art img-sp_sarn_gear k34" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, gear for The Sarn" style="background-size:cover"></div><figcaption>Heat bank</figcaption></figure></div>
<div class="sptext"><h4>The Sarn</h4><p class="tag">Barely needs a suit</p><dl><div><dt>Body</dt><dd>A four armed crystal, born in vacuum.</dd></div><div><dt>The suit</dt><dd>Gold foil fins and a lantern of stored heat, because cold slows it down.</dd></div><div><dt>In play</dt><dd>Unlock class. Ignores vacuum. Strong cards burn Heat as fuel.</dd></div></dl></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s" id="ship-hexes" aria-label="Cold Salvage: ship hexes"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Ship hexes</p><h3>Four rules space adds</h3><p class="lead" style="margin-top:16px;font-size:18px">Everything else is Gloomhaven with new names.</p></div>
<div class="rtiles"><div class="rtile"><b>Hazard hexes</b><p>Vacuum, live current and frost hurt on entry.</p></div><div class="rtile"><b>Decompression</b><p>Open a breached hatch and every figure is dragged one hex toward it.</p></div><div class="rtile"><b>The air clock</b><p>A shared track on the board. When it runs out, the room is lost.</p></div><div class="rtile"><b>Spreading Rime</b><p>An enemy that never moves. It grows one hex a round toward the warmest suit.</p></div></div>
<div class="tbl" style="margin-top:40px"><table><thead><tr><th>Gloomhaven</th><th>Cold Salvage</th><th>Core change</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven">Initiative</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Boot number: a nimble suit patches before a heavy cutter swings.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven">Lost card</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Burned module: a strong routine fries part of the suit.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven">Exhaustion</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Suit dark: the hero is dragged back to the airlock.</td><td data-l="Core change">Wording only</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven">Attack modifier deck</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Fault deck: a null is a jam, a double is an overcharge.</td><td data-l="Core change">Renaming, held in data</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven">Rooms and doors</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Bulkheads: a breached compartment can vent.</td><td data-l="Core change">Pressure state per room, as scenario text</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p class="cap">We have not checked these against the current core build. Hazard hexes and forced movement are the two to confirm first.</p></div></section><section class="spread t-s boardpage" id="scenarios" aria-label="Cold Salvage: Scenario one: Cold Start"><div class="wrap"><div class="bhead"><p class="eyebrow">Scenario boards</p><h3>Every room is built for a fight</h3><p class="bsub"><b>Scenario one: Cold Start.</b> Push through the crawl, take the bay, shut down the reactor before the air runs out.</p></div>
<div class="ovscroll"><div class="ov" style="aspect-ratio:16/9"><div class="art img-s_lvl1 " role="img" aria-label="Concept art of scenario one: a maintenance crawl, a cargo bay with containers and a <div class="rintent"><div><b>Maintenance crawl <span>16 hexes</span></b><p>Two hexes wide from the airlock, then one hex wide for the last stretch before the bay hatch. One figure holds that line, and the Durr is the one you want there.</p></div><div><b>Cargo bay <span>90 hexes</span></b><p>Big and broken up by containers, so every stack is cover and a flank. The gantry trades safety for range.</p></div><div><b>Reactor hall <span>30 hexes</span></b><p>A ring around the core. Go left through frost and arrive slow, or right over burning vents and arrive hurt.</p></div></div>

Safe to loot, slow to leave.</p></div><div><b>Hull deck <span>128 hexes</span></b><p>Wide, exposed and pulled toward space. <div class="mcols"><div><b>How it plays</b><p>Finishing a scenario unlocks new numbered locations on the ring. Pick any open one and play it. Travel is flavour.</p></div><div><b>What it does well</b><p>Simple, and the story stays in our hands. In Gloomhaven, unlocked scenarios get a sticker on the map, and travel normally draws one road event (<a href="https://ultraboardgames.com/gloomhaven/campaign-overview.php">UltraBoardGames</a>, <a href="https://rules.dized.com/game/I7lEsCGOS2-zgol-ZRNf3g/vMMmX3sqR7qB6pqQFZJbSw/scenario-page-breakdown">Dized</a>).</p></div><div class="tr"><b>The trade-off</b><p>The map is a pretty menu. Where a location sits changes nothing, which is why this one felt meaningless.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s mapopt" id="map-b" aria-label="Campaign map option B"><div class="wrap"><div class="mhead"><div><p class="eyebrow">Campaign map, option B</p><h3>Route through the wreck</h3></div><span class="pill" style="color:#fff;background:#F2762E;border-color:#F2762E">Our recommendation</span></div>

<div class="mcols"><div><b>How it plays</b><p>Jump node to node, paying supply or air. Your sector sets hazards and loot. Run dry and you limp home, losing the haul.</p></div><div><b>What it does well</b><p>Every jump is a decision. Routes close as the ring decays, and some only open for a species, like the Durr hull jack.</p></div><div class="tr"><b>The trade-off</b><p>More to build and balance: an economy, route events and scenarios that must work in any order. Closer to the jump map in FTL than to Gloomhaven.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s" aria-label="Campaign map: A against B"><div class="wrap"><div class="grid2" style="gap:64px;align-items:center"><div><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Your call</p><h3>Option A or option B</h3></div><p class="swap">We would build option B. The art already promises a dying ring, and only B makes that promise cost you something.</p><p style="margin-top:18px;color:var(--muted)">If you want the tighter story, A ships sooner and can grow into B later.</p></div>
<div class="tbl vs"><table><thead><tr><th></th><th>A. Scenario picker</th><th>B. Route through the wreck</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Decision per jump</td><td>None</td><td class="w">Supply, air and risk</td></tr><tr><td>Story control</td><td class="w">Full</td><td>Branching, harder to write</td></tr><tr><td>Replay value</td><td>Low</td><td class="w">High</td></tr><tr><td>Build cost, our estimate</td><td class="w">Low</td><td>Medium to high</td></tr><tr><td>Uses the ring decay</td><td>As flavour</td><td class="w">As a rule</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s" aria-label="Cold Salvage: enemies"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Enemies</p><h3>Three factions</h3></div><div class="foes"><div><div class="art img-s_enemies k169" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, three enemy factions: Wardens, Rime and Brokers"></div><p class="cap">Concept art. Left to right: Wardens, Rime, Brokers.</p></div><div><div class="foe"><h4>Wardens</h4><p>The ring’s old security. Fixed patrols, nearest suit first, never retreat.</p></div><div class="foe"><h4>Rime</h4><p>Frost that feeds on warmth. Grows toward the hottest suit, so waiting loses.</p></div><div class="foe"><h4>Brokers</h4><p>Rival salvagers. Grab loot first, flee when outnumbered.</p></div></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s" aria-label="Cold Salvage: ability cards"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Ability cards</p><h3>Two Cutter cards</h3></div><div class="cardrow"><div><svg viewBox="0 0 300 440" role="img" aria-label="Ability card Arc Cut, initiative 18" style="font-family:var(--sans)">

Hull Breach is slow, strong, and burns out after one use.</p><p class="cap">Vector artwork with real text, on the Gloomhaven card layout.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-s" id="space-ask" aria-label="Cold Salvage: the ask"><div class="wrap"><div class="ask"><div><p class="eyebrow">The ask</p><p class="big" style="margin-top:18px">Let us build one sector.</p><p class="lead" style="margin-top:24px">A vertical slice on the rules core you already have. You judge it with the game in your hands, then decide on the rest.</p></div>
<ol><li>Four playable species: the Durr, humans, the Murmur and the Tikkri.</li><li>Three scenarios that use hazard hexes, decompression and the air clock.</li><li>One sector of the campaign map, built as option A or option B. You pick.</li><li>A build you can play on your own machine.</li></ol></div></div></section><section class="spread opener t-r" id="r"><div class="art cine img-r_key" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, key art for The Salt Road" style="background-position:50% 55%"></div>
<div class="wrap"><div class="body"><div><p class="eyebrow">Theme two. A caravan across a dead sea</p><h2>The Salt Road</h2><p class="lead">Four guides lead a caravan across the Hollow Sea, a salt basin where a vanished empire left glass towers, walking machines and a heat that never quite stops moving.</p><p class="tone"><b>Tone.</b> Warm, mythic and quiet. Hospitality is a virtue, and the danger arrives wearing beauty.</p><p class="cap">Concept art. Key art for The Salt Road.</p></div>
<ol class="pillars"><li><span class="numl">1</span><div><b>Water is the clock</b><span>The caravan's water stock is a campaign resource. Every scenario spends some, and running dry ends the story.</span></div></li><li><span class="numl">2</span><div><b>The road is the campaign</b><span>The hub is the caravan itself. It moves along a route you choose, and the next camp is never the last one.</span></div></li><li><span class="numl">3</span><div><b>Beauty with teeth</b><span>Mirages, glass towers and singing salt are lovely and lethal. Enemies look like landscape until they do not.</span></div></li></ol></div></div></section><section class="spread t-r" aria-label="The Salt Road: rules fit"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">The Salt Road</p><h3>How it fits the Gloomhaven rules</h3></div><div class="rules"><div class="tbl"><table><thead><tr><th>Gloomhaven system</th><th>In this theme</th><th>Core change</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Initiative from the leading card</td><td data-l="In this theme">Pace. Each card sets how early in the heat you act. The lowest number steps first.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Top and bottom halves, default Attack 2 and Move 2</td><td data-l="In this theme">Cards are crafts and songs. The fallback is the plain work of the road: a staff strike and a few steps.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Lost cards</td><td data-l="In this theme">Water spent. A powerful card empties a gourd for the rest of the scenario.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Exhaustion</td><td data-l="In this theme">Thirst. With no cards left, the hero collapses and the caravan carries them out.</td><td data-l="Core change">Wording only</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Short and long rests</td><td data-l="In this theme">Short rest is a drink in the shade, and a random card spills. Long rest is making camp, where the player chooses what to give up.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Attack modifier deck</td><td data-l="In this theme">The wind deck. A null is dead calm or a blown shot, a double is a tailwind. Bless and curse are fair wind and ill omen.</td><td data-l="Core change">Renaming, held in data</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Monster ability decks and focus</td><td data-l="In this theme">Mirage kin shimmer and flee. Glass sentinels patrol fixed routes. Reavers ride in coordinated raids and target the weakest.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Loot</td><td data-l="In this theme">Trade goods and glass shards on the board. Water and goods at the hub.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Rooms and doors</td><td data-l="In this theme">Gates and courtyards. Opening a gate reveals the next courtyard of a ruined caravanserai.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<div><p class="small" style="margin-bottom:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--accent)">Requests for the rules core</p><ul class="reqs"><li><b>Wind direction</b><span>An optional round marker that nudges forced movement. A scenario rule, not a core rule.</span></li><li><b>Terrain data</b><span>Sinkholes, glass floors and dunes as terrain types. Every theme here needs terrain as data.</span></li><li><b>Campaign layer</b><span>Water stock between scenarios. This lives outside the scenario rules entirely.</span></li></ul><p class="small" style="margin-top:16px">We have not checked these requests against the current core build. Treat them as a list to confirm with the engineers.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="spread mapspread t-r" aria-label="The Salt Road: campaign map"><div class="art img-r_map sq k169" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, campaign map for The Salt Road" style="background-position:50% 50%;aspect-ratio:1280/560"></div><div class="wrap"><div class="mapcap"><div><p class="eyebrow">The Salt Road: campaign</p><h3>The campaign map</h3><p class="cap">Concept art. The campaign map: the Hollow Sea drawn as a traveller's chart, with the three roads of the first leg.</p></div><div><p class="lead" style="font-size:18px">The caravan crosses the Hollow Sea in three legs. Each leg offers three roads, and the road you take decides which allies and enemies you meet.</p><dl style="margin-top:24px"><div><dt>Hub</dt><dd>The caravan camp. It moves along the route, and each camp has different trade, shelter and rumours.</dd></div><div><dt>Clock</dt><dd>The dry season. Water spent on scenarios is water not carried, and the flood season is coming.</dd></div></dl></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-r" aria-label="The Salt Road: branching"><div <ul class="notes"><li><b>Pace track on top</b><span>The order of the day, with heroes and enemies in one strip. A brass outline marks whose turn it is.</span></li><li><b>Omens as the weather</b><span>Sun, wind and water counters sit beside the track, so the day's conditions are always in view.</span></li><li><b>Hand along the bottom</b><span>Parchment style cards in the same layout as every other theme. The layout is theme agnostic; only the dress changes.</span></li></ul></div></div></section><section class="spread t-r" aria-label="The Salt Road: heroes"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">The Salt Road</p><h3>Four starter heroes</h3></div><div class="grid4"><article class="hero"><div class="art img-r_h1 " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Wayguard"></div><span class="n">Hero 1</span><h4>Wayguard</h4><p class="role">Frontline. Shield bearer who keeps the caravan's flank closed.</p><p class="sig"><b>Signature mechanic.</b> Shield wall: spends a lost card to turn adjacent allies' damage into water loss instead of health loss.</p></article><article class="hero"><div class="art img-r_h2 " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Glass Singer"></div><span class="n">Hero 2</span><h4>Glass Singer</h4><p class="role">Ranged damage. Shapes shards of glass with sound.</p><p class="sig"><b>Signature mechanic.</b> Resonance: each song adds a shard to the board, and a later song can shatter all shards at once.</p></article><article class="hero"><div class="art img-r_h3 " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Wellkeeper"></div><span class="n">Hero 3</span><h4>Wellkeeper</h4><p class="role">Healer and support. Carries the caravan's water.</p><p class="sig"><b>Signature mechanic.</b> Dowsing: heals by pouring from the caravan's water stock, so healing has a campaign cost.</p></article><article class="hero"><div class="art img-r_h4 " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Sandfoot"></div><span class="n">Hero 4</span><h4>Sandfoot</h4><p class="role">Scout and archer. First across every dune.</p><p class="sig"><b>Signature mechanic.</b> Light step: ignores sand and glass terrain, and can place a rope line that others move along for free.</p></article></div><p class="cap" style="margin-top:32px">Concept art. Left to right: Wayguard, Glass Singer, Wellkeeper, Sandfoot.</p></div></section><section class="spread t-r" aria-label="The Salt Road: enemies"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">The Salt Road</p><h3>Three enemy factions</h3></div><div class="foes"><div><div class="art img-r_enemies k169" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, three enemy factions for The Salt Road"></div><p class="cap">Concept art. Left to right: Mirage kin, Glass sentinel, a Reaver on a salt beetle.</p></div><div><div class="foe"><h4>Mirage kin</h4><p>Spirits of the lost, which look like heat shimmer.</p><p class="b">Drift toward the hero with the most water, and flee when seen. Hard to pin down, easy to scare.</p></div><div class="foe"><h4>Glass sentinels</h4><p>The old empire's walking machines.</p><p class="b">Fixed patrol routines. Slow, deliberate and heavily armoured, and they turn light into damage.</p></div><div class="foe"><h4>Reavers</h4><p>Raiders who ride giant beetles across the flats.</p><p class="b">Coordinated raids on the weakest hero, and they steal water when they win.</p></div></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-r" aria-label="The Salt Road: ability cards"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">The Salt Road</p><h3>Two sample ability cards</h3></div><div class="cardrow"><div><svg viewBox="0 0 300 440" role="img" aria-label="Ability card Pitch of Dawn, initiative 24" style="font-family:var(--sans)">

</svg></div><div><p style="font-size:17px;margin-bottom:20px">The Glass Singer's first two cards. Pitch of Dawn is a quick ranged note. Shatter Chord is a slow chord that costs a lost card.</p><ul class="anat"><li><b>Name</b> on the banner, with the initiative number on the ring at the divider.</li><li><b>Upper and lower actions</b> are the two halves of the card, played in either order.</li><li><b>The stepped divider</b> shows which half each basic action replaces. The left Attack 2 tab hangs from the bottom edge of the top half. The right Move 2 tab rises from the top edge of the bottom half. The initiative ring sits on the step between them.</li><li><b>Flame</b> marks a card that is lost when played. <b>Star</b> shows experience gained.</li></ul><p class="cap">Drawn as vector artwork with real text, following the Gloomhaven card layout.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-r" aria-label="The Salt Road: risks"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">The Salt Road</p><h3>Risks and open questions</h3></div><div class="riskgrid"><ul class="risks"><li><div><b>Cultural sourcing</b><span>A desert caravan invites borrowing from real cultures. Frosthaven's creator changed aspects of its setting to address cultural bias, according to the Gloomhaven article we cite below. We would invent our own cultures and bring in outside reviewers.</span></div><span class="pill hi">High</span></li><li><div><b>Desert sameness</b><span>Tan and white across a long campaign gets dull. Glass canyons, flood plains, oases and mountain passes carry the colour range, and the concept art here already shows it.</span></div><span class="pill md">Medium</span></li><li><div><b>Fewer iconic enemies</b><span>Space and sea have clear monsters. The desert needs its enemies to be strange, such as the mirage kin, or they read as generic raiders.</span></div><span class="pill md">Medium</span></li><li><div><b>Cloth and ornament cost</b><span>Robes, patterns and architecture are harder to model and animate well than hard surfaces. This is a team estimate, not a measured cost.</span></div><span class="pill md">Medium</span></li></ul><div class="oq"><h4>Open questions</h4><ol><li>Can a moving hub feel as substantial as a fixed outpost like Frosthaven's?</li><li>Who reviews the cultures we invent, and when do they join?</li><li>Is the water stock a real campaign resource, or a bookkeeping task players will skip?</li></ol></div></div></div></section><section class="spread opener t-t" id="t"><div class="art cine img-t_key" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, key art for Tidewatch" style="background-position:50% 55%"></div>
<div class="wrap"><div class="body"><div><p class="eyebrow">Theme three. A drowned coast</p><h2>Tidewatch</h2><p class="lead">The lamps along the Hollow Coast are going out. Four keepers walk the tideline to relight them before the fog arrives with what the sea took.</p><p class="tone"><b>Tone.</b> Eerie, quiet folk horror. Hearth warmth against a dark that is patient and close.</p><p class="cap">Concept art. Key art for Tidewatch.</p></div>
<ol class="pillars"><li><span class="numl">1</span><div><b>Light is life</b><span>Lamps are objectives, safe zones and the campaign's progress bar. Where the light reaches, the fog cannot.</span></div></li><li><span class="numl">2</span><div><b>The tide changes the board</b><span>Flood and ebb rewrite the map between rounds. A hex that was safe is underwater, and a drowned path is open.</span></div></li><li><span class="numl">3</span><div><b>Small, human and haunted</b><span>Keepers, fishers and villagers. No chosen ones, only people who decided not to look away.</span></div></li></ol></div></div></section><section class="spread t-t" aria-label="Tidewatch: rules fit"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Tidewatch</p><h3>How it fits the Gloomhaven rules</h3></div><div class="rules"><div class="tbl"><table><thead><tr><th>Gloomhaven system</th><th>In this theme</th><th>Core change</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Initiative from the leading card</td><td data-l="In this theme">Watch order. Each card sets when in the watch you act. The lowest number goes first.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Top and bottom halves, default Attack 2 and Move 2</td><td data-l="In this theme">Cards are habits of the watch. The fallback is the plain work of the coast: a hook strike and a few steps.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Lost cards</td><td data-l="In this theme">Wick burned down. A powerful card consumes oil that cannot be reused until a long rest.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Exhaustion</td><td data-l="In this theme">Taken by the tide. A keeper who cannot hold the watch loses their lamp and walks into the fog.</td><td data-l="Core change">Wording only</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Short and long rests</td><td data-l="In this theme">Short rest trims the wick, and a random card burns out. Long rest is keeping vigil by a lamp, where the player chooses what burns.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Attack modifier deck</td><td data-l="In this theme">The tide deck. A null is slack water, a double is a rogue wave. Bless and curse are fair wind and ill omen.</td><td data-l="Core change">Renaming, held in data</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Monster ability decks and focus</td><td data-l="In this theme">The Choir pulls heroes toward the water. Wreckwrought hulks plod and hit hard. Gullbone swarms scatter and regroup.</td><td data-l="Core change">Pull as a first class forced move</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Loot</td><td data-l="In this theme">Wreckage and wrack on the board. Salvage and oil at the hub.</td><td data-l="Core change">None</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Gloomhaven system">Rooms and doors</td><td data-l="In this theme">Lighthouse chambers, cellars and boat sheds. Opening a door can let the tide in.</td><td data-l="Core change">Tide state per room, written as scenario text</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<div><p class="small" style="margin-bottom:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--accent)">Requests for the rules core</p><ul class="reqs"><li><b>Scheduled terrain change</b><span>Flood and ebb change which hexes are open, on a fixed schedule per scenario. This is a new core feature, and the largest ask of the three themes.</span></li><li><b>Moving fog</b><span>Fog hexes block line of sight and advance each round. Fog is a hazard type with a movement rule.</span></li><li><b>Forced movement</b><span>The Choir pulls heroes toward the water, and Harpooner pulls enemies back.</span></li><li><b>Light radius</b><span>Lamps change what counts as visible. This could be interface only, which needs confirming.</span></li></ul><p class="small" style="margin-top:16px">We have not checked these requests against the current core build. Treat them as a list to confirm with the engineers.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="spread mapspread t-t" aria-label="Tidewatch: campaign map"><div class="art img-t_map sq k169" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, campaign map for Tidewatch" style="background-position:50% 50%;aspect-ratio:1280/560"></div><div class="wrap"><div class="mapcap"><div><p class="eyebrow">Tidewatch: campaign</p><h3>The campaign map</h3><p class="cap">Concept art. The campaign map: the Hollow Coast as a navigator's chart, with lamp towers marked along the shore.</p></div><div><p class="lead" style="font-size:18px">A chain of five lighthouses stands along the coast. The fog advances from the west each act, and every tower the keepers skip goes dark for good.</p><dl style="margin-top:24px"><div><dt>Hub</dt><dd>The keeper's lighthouse. It grows a new room for each lamp relit, and a lamp lost leaves a visible dark window.</dd></div><div><dt>Clock</dt><dd>The Long Fog advances one tower each act. Skipping a tower buys time and costs the town behind it.</dd></div></dl></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-t" aria-label="Tidewatch: branching"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p An amber outline marks whose turn it is.</span></li><li><b>Omens as weather</b><span>Light, flood and song counters sit beside the track, so the tide and fog state are always in view.</span></li><li><b>Hand along the bottom</b><span>The same layout as every other theme, dressed in weathered wood and rope.</span></li></ul></div></div></section><section class="spread t-t" aria-label="Tidewatch: heroes"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Tidewatch</p><h3>Four starter heroes</h3></div><div class="grid4"><article class="hero"><div class="art img-t_h1 " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Ballast"></div><span class="n">Hero 1</span><h4>Ballast</h4><p class="role">Frontline. Anchors the line and drags enemies back.</p><p class="sig"><b>Signature mechanic.</b> Chain anchor: pins an enemy in place, and pinned enemies cannot be pulled by the Choir.</p></article><article class="hero"><div class="art img-t_h2 " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Harpooner"></div><span class="n">Hero 2</span><h4>Harpooner</h4><p class="role">Ranged damage and control. Hooks and reels.</p><p class="sig"><b>Signature mechanic.</b> Reel: pulls a target toward him, and a pull into a pool of flood water adds damage.</p></article><article class="hero"><div class="art img-t_h3 " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Lamplighter"></div><span class="n">Hero 3</span><h4>Lamplighter</h4><p class="role">Healer and light bearer. Keeps the fog at bay.</p><p class="sig"><b>Signature mechanic.</b> Light: places a Light on the board that heals allies inside it and holds back fog hexes.</p></article><article class="hero"><div class="art img-t_h4 " role="img" aria-label="Concept art, Stiltwalker"></div><span class="n">Hero 4</span><h4>Stiltwalker</h4><p class="role">Scout and trickster. Walks above the flood on stilts.</p><p class="sig"><b>Signature mechanic.</b> High ground: ignores water terrain and sees over fog, but loses the bonus if knocked down.</p></article></div><p class="cap" style="margin-top:32px">Concept art. Left to right: Ballast, Harpooner, Lamplighter, Stiltwalker.</p></div></section><section class="spread t-t" aria-label="Tidewatch: enemies"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Tidewatch</p><h3>Three enemy factions</h3></div><div class="foes"><div><div class="art img-t_enemies k169" role="img" aria-label="Concept art, three enemy factions for Tidewatch"></div><p class="cap">Concept art. Left to right: the Choir, a Wreckwrought hulk, a Gullbone swarm.</p></div><div><div class="foe"><h4>The Choir</h4><p>Drowned villagers who sing the living toward the water.</p><p class="b">Stay back and pull the nearest hero one hex closer to the water each round.</p></div><div class="foe"><h4>Wreckwrought</h4><p>Hulks of wreckage and rust that walk the shore.</p><p class="b">Slow fixed patrol that hits very hard. They cannot cross lamp light.</p></div><div class="foe"><h4>Gullbone swarm</h4><p>A cloud of bone and feather.</p><p class="b">Scatter when hit and regroup at the end of each round. Hard to finish, easy to hurt.</p></div></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-t" aria-label="Tidewatch: ability cards"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Tidewatch</p><h3>Two sample ability cards</h3></div><div class="cardrow"><div><svg viewBox="0 0 300 440" role="img" aria-label="Ability card Trim the Wick, initiative 31" style="font-family:var(--sans)">

Last Lantern is a slow, powerful heal that burns out.</p><ul class="anat"><li><b>Name</b> on the banner, with the initiative number on the ring at the divider.</li><li><b>Upper and lower actions</b> are the two halves of the card, played in either order.</li><li><b>The stepped divider</b> shows which half each basic action replaces. The left Attack 2 tab hangs from the bottom edge of the top half. The right Move 2 tab rises from the top edge of the bottom half. The initiative ring sits on the step between them.</li><li><b>Flame</b> marks a card that is lost when played. <b>Star</b> shows experience gained.</li></ul><p class="cap">Drawn as vector artwork with real text, following the Gloomhaven card layout.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-t" aria-label="Tidewatch: risks"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Tidewatch</p><h3>Risks and open questions</h3></div><div class="riskgrid"><ul class="risks"><li><div><b>Rules and rendering cost</b><span>Tide and fog are the largest core change here and the most expensive art. Water, wet surfaces and volumetric fog are the hardest of the three themes to render, and this is our estimate, not a measured cost.</span></div><span class="pill hi">High</span></li><li><div><b>Dynamic terrain complexity</b><span>Scheduled flooding is easy to explain and hard to balance. Scenarios would need to be designed around the schedule from the start.</span></div><span class="pill hi">High</span></li><li><div><b>Horror fatigue</b><span>Folk horror works in small doses. A long campaign needs warm hub scenes or the mood becomes a drone.</span></div><span class="pill md">Medium</span></li><li><div><b>Echoes of familiar monsters</b><span>Drowned dead can read as generic undead. The Choir's pull and song are meant to avoid that, but the risk is real.</span></div><span class="pill md">Medium</span></li></ul><div class="oq"><h4>Open questions</h4><ol><li>Is the core willing to take a scheduled terrain feature, or must tide be written as scenario text?</li><li>How do we communicate the next tide state without cluttering the board?</li><li>Can the art pipeline hold a consistent water look at an acceptable cost?</li></ol></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-p" id="compare"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Side by side</p><h2>The three themes compared</h2><p class="lead" style="margin-top:16px;font-size:18px">Every rating is our judgement. There are no playtests, and none of this has been measured.</p></div>
<div class="tbl"><table><thead><tr><th>Dimension</th><th>Cold Salvage</th><th>The Salt Road</th><th>Tidewatch</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td data-l="Dimension">Tone</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Quiet industrial dread</td><td data-l="The Salt Road">Warm mythic awe</td><td data-l="Tidewatch">Eerie folk horror</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Dimension">Strongest rule translation</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Exhaustion as suit power, doors as pressure</td><td data-l="The Salt Road">Exhaustion as thirst, campaign as a route</td><td data-l="Tidewatch">The tide rewrites the board</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Dimension">Changes to the core</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Few: hazard hexes and forced movement</td><td data-l="The Salt Road">Fewest: optional wind marker</td><td data-l="Tidewatch">Most: scheduled terrain and moving fog</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Dimension">Art cost (team estimate)</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Lowest: hard surfaces, modular kits</td><td data-l="The Salt Road">Middle: cloth, ornament, architecture</td><td data-l="Tidewatch">Highest: water, fog, wet surfaces</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Dimension">Market crowding (from the games we found)</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Highest: several space tactics games in our sources</td><td data-l="The Salt Road">Lowest: we found no close match</td><td data-l="Tidewatch">Middle: sea horror exists in other genres</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Dimension">Campaign hook</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Ship hub plus a decaying ring</td><td data-l="The Salt Road">Moving caravan plus a water stock</td><td data-l="Tidewatch">Lighthouse chain plus advancing fog</td></tr><tr><td data-l="Dimension">Biggest risk</td><td data-l="Cold Salvage">Reads as fantasy with lasers</td><td data-l="The Salt Road">Cultural sourcing and desert sameness</td><td data-l="Tidewatch">Rule and render cost of tide and fog</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></section>
<section class="spread t-p" aria-label="Where the themes land"><div class="wrap"><div class="matrixwrap"><svg viewBox="0 0 640 420" role="img" aria-label="Chart placing the three themes by how distinctive they are and how easily they fit the rules core" class="matrix"><rect x="60" y="20" width="560" height="350" rx="10" fill="var(--panel)" stroke="var(--line)"/><line x1="340" y1="20" x2="340" y2="370" stroke="var(--line)" stroke-dasharray="4 5"/><line x1="60" y1="195" x2="620" y2="195" stroke="var(--line)" stroke-dasharray="4 5"/><circle cx="172" cy="153" r="9" fill="#F2762E" stroke="var(--bg)" stroke-width="3"/><text x="188" y="153" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="central" class="mlabel">Cold Salvage</text><circle cx="519.2" cy="72.5" r="9" fill="#8C6420" stroke="var(--bg)" stroke-width="3"/><text x="503.20000000000005" y="72.5" text-anchor="end" dominant-baseline="central" class="mlabel">The Salt Road</text><circle cx="429.6" cy="293" r="9" fill="#3E8F81" stroke="var(--bg)" stroke-width="3"/><text x="445.6" y="293" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="central" class="mlabel">Tidewatch</text><text x="60" y="402" class="maxis" dominant-baseline="central">Familiar</text><text x="620" y="402" class="maxis" text-anchor="end" dominant-baseline="central">Distinctive</text><text transform="translate(22 370) rotate(-90)" class="maxis" dominant-baseline="central">Costly core fit</text><text transform="translate(22 20) rotate(-90)" class="maxis" text-anchor="end" dominant-baseline="central">Easy core fit</text></svg><div><p class="eyebrow">Where the themes land</p><p class="verdict" style="margin-top:20px">On distinctiveness and core fit alone, the Salt Road wins. Space wins on art cost, enemy variety and how many players already understand it. That tension is the heart of the decision.</p><ul class="legend"><li><i style="background:#F2762E"></i>Cold Salvage</li><li><i style="background:#8C6420"></i>The Salt Road</li><li><i style="background:#3E8F81"></i>Tidewatch</li></ul><p class="cap">Placement is team judgement, not a measurement.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="spread t-p" id="comparables" aria-label="Comparable games"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Comparable games</p><h2>What other games tell us</h2><p class="lead" style="margin-top:16px;font-size:18px">Facts come from the linked sources. The last column is our reading.</p></div><div class="tbl"><table><thead><tr><th>Game</th><th>What the source says</th><th>What it means for Haven</th><th>Source</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td data-l="Game">Gloomhaven</td><td data-l="What the source says">95 scenarios, 17 classes, hex tiles, a two card turn and a modifier deck instead of dice.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">The baseline Haven must honour and then differ from.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloomhaven">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Frosthaven</td><td data-l="What the source says">An outpost setting. Raised almost 13 million dollars from over 83,000 backers. Its creator changed aspects of the setting to address cultural bias.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">A growing hub works. A setting borrowed from real cultures draws scrutiny.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloomhaven">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Jaws of the Lion</td><td data-l="What the source says">A standalone game with 25 scenarios, including 5 tutorial scenarios.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">A teaching arc is worth its own scenarios.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloomhaven">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Gloomhaven Digital</td><td data-l="What the source says">A 95 mission campaign plus 160 or more Guildmaster missions. Its store page warns that cards are as scarce as health.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">Digital removes bookkeeping. Card scarcity is the heart of the game.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/780290/Gloomhaven/">store.steampowered.com</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Slay the Spire</td><td data-l="What the source says">Roguelike deck building. Enemies telegraph their next move, and the run is a branching map of encounters.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">Telegraphed intent and a branching map are proven, readable structures.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slay_the_Spire">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Into the Breach</td><td data-l="What the source says">Turn based tactics on a small grid. Enemy attacks are telegraphed, and pushing enemies is central. A power grid is something to protect.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">Forced movement and a thing to protect make a small space game feel distinct.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Into_the_Breach">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Hoplite</td><td data-l="What the source says">Turn based tactics on a hex arena where lava pools are instantly fatal.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">A clear hazard hex is enough to change how a board is played.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoplite_(video_game)">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></section><section class="spread t-p cont"  aria-label="Comparable games"><div class="wrap"><div class="tbl"><table><thead><tr><th>Game</th><th>What the source says</th><th>What it means for Haven</th><th>Source</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td data-l="Game">FTL: Faster Than Light</td><td data-l="What the source says">A ship's crew jumping across eight sectors, with a rebel fleet advancing as you go.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">A pursuing clock gives a campaign a spine. The ship as a home is a strong frame.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTL:_Faster_Than_Light">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">XCOM: Enemy Unknown</td><td data-l="What the source says">Turn based tactics with cover, and a base you return to between missions.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">Cover and a base between missions are the standard for a reason.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XCOM:_Enemy_Unknown">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Imperial Assault</td><td data-l="What the source says">One Imperial player against up to four heroes. Two actions each, and a branching campaign.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">Space adjacent tabletop is already crowded, and it is competitive, not cooperative.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://www.fantasyflightgames.com/product/star-wars-imperial-assault/">fantasyflightgames.com</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Nemesis</td><td data-l="What the source says">A semi cooperative game of 15 turns, criticised for its complexity and length.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">A caution on space horror: do not let rules overwhelm the mood.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemesis_(board_game)">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Phantom Epoch</td><td data-l="What the source says">A cooperative tactical board game with a 40 plus mission campaign blending sci fi and fantasy.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">A direct Gloomhaven style rival in space.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://www.boardgamevideo.com/videos/phantom-epoch-or-a-gloomhaven-styled-space-opera-or-kickstarter-preview-IAER4YYM0cY">boardgamevideo.com</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Clonizer</td><td data-l="What the source says">A space game that combines hex tactics and roguelike deck building, released 14 April 2025.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">Hex tactics and cards in space is not a new idea.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://www.vgdb.co/games/clonizer">vgdb.co</a></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></section><section class="spread t-p cont"  aria-label="Comparable games"><div class="wrap"><div class="tbl"><table><thead><tr><th>Game</th><th>What the source says</th><th>What it means for Haven</th><th>Source</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td data-l="Game">Rogue Angels</td><td data-l="What the source says">A cooperative sci fi adventure with multiple paths. Its site compares itself to Gloomhaven.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">Another space entrant claiming the same neighbourhood.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://www.suntzugames.com/rogue-angels">suntzugames.com</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Stars of Akarios</td><td data-l="What the source says">A video review calls it basically Gloomhaven in space.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">More of the same crowd.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://www.boardgamevideo.com/videos/stars-of-akarios-unboxing-and-rambling-basically-gloomhaven-in-space-ek5o9HMpBgg">boardgamevideo.com</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Rogue Vector</td><td data-l="What the source says">A sci fi roguelike deck builder where every ship moves at once.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">A different take on cards in space, worth watching.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://chaostheorygames.itch.io/rogue-vector">chaostheorygames.itch.io</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">The Banner Saga</td><td data-l="What the source says">A story told through a caravan on a long journey.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">A caravan carries a narrative well. Relevant to the Salt Road.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Banner_Saga">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Dredge</td><td data-l="What the source says">A serene day and a horror night on the water.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">A clear model for light and dark shifts. Relevant to Tidewatch.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dredge_(video_game)">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr><tr><td data-l="Game">Sunless Sea</td><td data-l="What the source says">Slow ship movement used to build tension.</td><td data-l="What it means for Haven">Slow, dark water can carry tone. Relevant to Tidewatch.</td><td data-l="Source"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunless_Sea">en.wikipedia.org</a></td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="small" style="margin-top:20px">Clonizer and Rogue Vector were read from their store pages only, and we have not played either. The Stars of Akarios comparison comes from the title of one video review.</p></div></section><section class="spread t-p" id="recommendation"><div class="wrap"><div class="grid2" style="gap:72px"><div><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Our recommendation</p><h2>Cold Salvage, with a hedge</h2></div><p class="swap">Take Cold Salvage as the lead theme, and prove the core against The Salt Road at the same time.</p><p style="margin-top:20px;font-size:17px;color:var(--muted)">Space gives us the cheapest consistent art, the most obvious hub and an environment that can carry the rules. The Salt Road is the most distinctive theme and the safest check that the core is theme agnostic.</p>
<ul class="reqs" style="margin-top:40px"><li><b>Why not the Salt Road as the lead <span class="pill md" style="display:inline-flex;margin-left:8px">Runner up</span></b><span>Only because of cost and risk, not quality. Cloth and ornament are slower to produce well, and cultural sourcing needs review we have not arranged.</span></li><li><b>Why not Tidewatch as the lead <span class="pill md" style="display:inline-flex;margin-left:8px">Expansion candidate</span></b><span>It has the best atmosphere and the largest change to the rules core, plus the highest art cost. We would revisit it for an expansion.</span></li></ul></div>
<ol class="recsteps pcpad"><li><div><b>Run the swap test on five space scenario premises</b><span>On paper, before any art or code. Any premise that survives a fantasy swap is cut.</span></div></li><li><div><b>Build one scenario in Cold Salvage</b><span>A single compartment with air as the clock, using only the cards and rules the core has today.</span></div></li><li><div><b>Skin the same scenario data as the Salt Road</b><span>Same rules and data, new names and terrain. This tests the design check from the notes.</span></div></li><li><div><b>Compare and decide</b><span>If the space version only works because of laser guns, or cannot say anything that fantasy cannot, we switch the lead.</span></div></li></ol></div></div></section><section class="spread t-p" id="questions"><div class="wrap"><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">Questions for you</p><h2>Five questions that push back on the lean toward space</h2></div><ol class="qs"><li>If you could only keep one of the three, and space were off the table, which would you pick? If the answer is not space, why do you lean toward it?</li><li>Space asks for hazard hexes, forced movement and an air clock. Are you willing to accept theme led rules in the core, or must every theme be a pure skin? If it is a pure skin, we should be honest that Cold Salvage is fantasy with lasers.</li><li>Do you want guns to be strong? Players of space games expect them. Making them weak keeps the hex tactics interesting and may disappoint people who came for blasters.</li><li>Do you want dread, awe or warmth in the first ten minutes of play? Each theme gives a different answer, and the tone should drive the choice more than the mechanics.</li><li>How much risk are you willing to carry on art and review? Tidewatch costs the most to render and the Salt Road needs outside cultural review. Space is the cheapest. Are you choosing space because you want it, or because it is cheap?</li></ol></div></section><section class="spread t-p" id="sources"><div class="wrap"><div class="grid2" style="gap:72px"><div><div class="sh"><p class="eyebrow">How to read the art</p><h2>Concept art, not final art</h2></div><p style="font-size:17px">Every image in this readout is AI generated concept art, used as a mood board to set direction. None of it is final production art, and no text was generated inside any image. Interface mockups and ability cards are drawn as vector artwork with real text. No playtests have been run, and every rating is our own judgement.</p></div>

Frosthaven, Jaws of the Lion and the digital edition)</a><br><span>Wikipedia</span></li><li><a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/780290/Gloomhaven/">Gloomhaven on Steam</a><br><span>Steam</span></li><li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slay_the_Spire">Slay the Spire</a><br><span>Wikipedia</span></li><li><a
